text:
4-8. Here the writer speaks in view of God's declaration, warning the wicked. 
 
    Lift ... up the horn--to exalt power, here, of the wicked himself--that is, to be arrogant or self-elated.

title: Psalms 75:5
text: 5. speak ... neck--insolently.

title: Psalms 75:6
text: 6. promotion--literally, "a lifting up." God is the only right judge of merit.

title: Psalms 75:8
text:
8. in the hand ... a cup ... red--God's wrath often thus represented (compare  Isaiah 51:17  Jer 25:15). 
 
    but the dregs--literally, "surely the dregs, they shall drain it."

title: Psalms 75:9
text: 9, 10. Contrasted is the lot of the pious who will praise God, and, acting under His direction, will destroy the power of the wicked, and exalt that of the righteous.

title: Psalms 76:1
text:
Psalms 76:1-12 . On Neginoth--(See on  Psalms 3:8 , title). This Psalm commemorates what the preceding anticipates: God's deliverance of His people by a signal interposition of power against their enemies. The occasion was probably the events narrated in  II Kings 19:35 Isaiah 37:1-28 . (Compare  Psalms 46:1-11 ). 
 
    1, 2. These well-known terms denote God's people and Church and His intimate and glorious relations to them.

title: Psalms 76:2
text: 2. Salem-- ( Genesis 14:18 ) is Jerusalem.

title: Psalms 76:3
text:
3. brake ... the arrows--literally, "thunderbolts" ( Psalms 78:48 ), from their rapid flight or ignition (compare  Psalms 18:14 Ephesians 6:16 ). 
 
    the battle--for arms ( Hosea 2:18 ).

title: Psalms 76:4
text:
4. Thou--God. 
 
    mountains of prey--great victorious nations, as Assyria ( Isaiah 41:15 Ezekiel 38:11 Ezekiel 38:12 Zechariah 4:7 ).

title: Psalms 76:5
text:
5. slept their sleep--died ( Psalms 13:3 ). 
 
    none ... found ... hands--are powerless.

title: Psalms 76:6
text: 6. chariot and horse--for those fighting on them (compare  Psalms 68:17 ).

title: Psalms 76:7
text: 7. may ... sight--contend with Thee ( Deuteronomy 9:4 Joshua 7:12 ).

title: Psalms 76:8
text: 8, 9. God's judgment on the wicked is His people's deliverance ( Psalms 9:12 Psalms 10:7 ).

title: Psalms 76:10
text:
10. Man's wrath praises God by its futility before His power. 
 
    restrain--or, "gird"; that is, Thyself, as with a sword, with which to destroy, or as an ornament to Thy praise.

title: Psalms 76:11
text: 11, 12. Invite homage to such a God ( II Chronicles 32:23 ), who can stop the breath of kings and princes when He wills ( Daniel 5:23 ).

title: Psalms 77:1
text:
Psalms 77:1-20 . To Jeduthun--(See on  Psalms 38:22 , title). In a time of great affliction, when ready to despair, the Psalmist derives relief from calling to mind God's former and wonderful works of delivering power and grace. 
 
    1. expresses the purport of the Psalm.

title: Psalms 77:2
text:
2. his importunacy. 
 
    my sore ran ... night--literally, "my hand was spread," or, "stretched out" (compare  Psalms 44:20 ). 
 
    ceased not--literally, "grew not numb," or, "feeble" ( Genesis 45:26 Psalms 38:8 ). 
 
    my soul ... comforted--(compare  Genesis 37:35 Jeremiah 31:15 ).

title: Psalms 77:3
text:
3-9. His sad state contrasted with former joys. 
 
    was troubled--literally, "violently agitated," or disquieted ( Psalms 39:6 Psalms 41:5 ). 
 
    my spirit was overwhelmed--or, "fainted" ( Psalms 107:5 Jonah 2:7 ).

title: Psalms 77:4
text: 4. holdest ... waking--or, "fast," that I cannot sleep. Thus he is led to express his anxious feelings in several earnest questions indicative of impatient sorrow.

title: Psalms 77:10
text: 10. Omitting the supplied words, we may read, "This is my affliction--the years of," &c., "years" being taken as parallel to affliction (compare  Psalms 90:15 ), as of God's ordering.

title: Psalms 77:11
text: 11, 12. He finds relief in contrasting God's former deliverances. Shall we receive good at His hands, and not evil? Both are orderings of unerring mercy and unfailing love.

title: Psalms 77:13
text: 13. Thy way ... in the sanctuary--God's ways of grace and providence ( Psalms 22:3 Psalms 67:2 ), ordered on holy principles, as developed in His worship; or implied in His perfections, if "holiness" be used for "sanctuary," as some prefer translating (compare  Exodus 15:11 ).

title: Psalms 77:14
text: 14-20. Illustrations of God's power in His special interventions for His people ( Exodus 14:1-31 ), and, in the more common, but sublime, control of nature ( Psalms 22:11-14 Habakkuk 3:14 ) which may have attended those miraculous events ( Exodus 14:24 ).

title: Psalms 77:15
text: 15. Jacob and Joseph--representing all.

title: Psalms 77:19
text: 19. waters ... , footsteps--may refer to His actual leading the people through the sea, though also expressing the mysteries of providence.

title: Psalms 78:1
text:
Psalms 78:1-72 . This Psalm appears to have been occasioned by the removal of the sanctuary from Shiloh in the tribe of Ephraim to Zion in the tribe of Judah, and the coincident transfer of pre-eminence in Israel from the former to the latter tribe, as clearly evinced by David's settlement as the head of the Church and nation. Though this was the execution of God's purpose, the writer here shows that it also proceeded from the divine judgment on Ephraim, under whose leadership the people had manifested the same sinful and rebellious character which had distinguished their ancestors in Egypt. 
 
    1. my people ... my law--the language of a religious teacher ( Psalms 78:2 Lamentations 3:14 Romans 2:16 Romans 2:27 ; compare  Psalms 49:4 ). The history which follows was a "dark saying," or riddle, if left unexplained, and its right apprehension required wisdom and attention.

title: Psalms 78:3
text: 3-8. This history had been handed down ( Exodus 12:14 Deuteronomy 6:20 ) for God's honor, and that the principles of His law might be known and observed by posterity. This important sentiment is reiterated in ( Psalms 78:7 Psalms 78:8 ) negative form.

title: Psalms 78:5
text: 5. testimony-- ( Psalms 19:7 ).

title: Psalms 78:8
text:
8. stubborn and rebellious-- ( Deuteronomy 21:1 ). 
 
    set not their heart--on God's service ( II Chronicles 12:14 ).

title: Psalms 78:9
text: 9-11. The privileges of the first-born which belonged to Joseph ( I Chronicles 5:1 I Chronicles 5:2 ) were assigned to Ephraim by Jacob ( Genesis 48:1 ). The supremacy of the tribe thus intimated was recognized by its position (in the marching of the nation to Canaan) next to the ark ( Numbers 2:18-24 ), by the selection of the first permanent locality for the ark within its borders at Shiloh, and by the extensive and fertile province given for its possession. Traces of this prominence remained after the schism under Rehoboam, in the use, by later writers, of Ephraim for Israel (compare  Hosea 5:3-14 Hosea 11:3-12 ). Though a strong, well-armed tribe, and, from an early period, emulous and haughty (compare  Joshua 17:14 Judges 8:1-3 II Samuel 19:41 ), it appears, in this place, that it had rather led the rest in cowardice than courage; and had incurred God's displeasure, because, diffident of His promise, though often heretofore fulfilled, it had failed as a leader to carry out the terms of the covenant, by not driving out the heathen ( Exodus 23:24 Deuteronomy 31:16 II Kings 17:15 ).

title: Psalms 78:12
text:
12-14. A record of God's dealings and the sins of the people is now made. The writer gives the history from the exode to the retreat from Kadesh; then contrasts their sins with their reasons for confidence, shown by a detail of God's dealings in Egypt, and presents a summary of the subsequent history to David's time. 
 
    Zoan--for Egypt, as its ancient capital ( Numbers 13:22 Isaiah 19:11 ).

title: Psalms 78:15
text:
15, 16. There were two similar miracles ( Exodus 17:6 Numbers 20:11 ). 
 
    great depths--and--rivers--denote abundance.

title: Psalms 78:17
text:
17-20. yet more--literally, "added to sin," instead of being led to repentance ( Romans 2:4 ). 
 
    provoking--and--tempted--illustrated by their absurd doubts,

title: Psalms 78:18
text:
18. in their heart-- ( Matthew 15:19 ). 
 
    for their lust--literally, "soul," or, "desire."

title: Psalms 78:19
text: 19, 20. in the face of His admitted power.

title: Psalms 78:21
text: 21. fire--the effect of the "anger" ( Numbers 11:1 ).

title: Psalms 78:22
text: 22. (Compare  Hebrews 8:8 Hebrews 8:9 ).

title: Psalms 78:23
text: 23-29. (Compare  Exodus 16:11-15 Numbers 11:4-9 ).

title: Psalms 78:25
text:
25. angels' food--literally, "bread of the mighty" (compare  Psalms 105:40 ); so called, as it came from heaven. 
 
    meat--literally, "victuals," as for a journey.

title: Psalms 78:29
text: 29. their ... desire--what they longed for.

title: Psalms 78:30
text: 30, 31. not estranged ... lust--or, "desire"--that is, were indulging it.

title: Psalms 78:31
text:
31. slew ... fattest--or, "among the fattest"; some of them-- 
 
    chosen--the young and strong ( Isaiah 40:31 ), and so none could resist.

title: Psalms 78:33
text: 33-39. Though there were partial reformations after chastisement, and God, in pity, withdrew His hand for a time, yet their general conduct was rebellious, and He was thus provoked to waste and destroy them, by long and fruitless wandering in the desert.

title: Psalms 78:36
text: 36. lied ... tongues--a feigned obedience ( Psalms 18:44 ).

title: Psalms 78:37
text: 37. heart ... not right--or, "firm" (compare  Psalms 78:8 Psalms 51:10 ).

title: Psalms 78:39
text: 39. a wind ... again--literally, "a breath," thin air (compare  Psalms 103:16 James 4:14 ).

title: Psalms 78:40
text: 40, 41. There were ten temptations ( Numbers 14:22 ).

title: Psalms 78:41
text:
41. limited--as in  Psalms 78:19 Psalms 78:20 . Though some prefer "grieved" or "provoked." The retreat from Kadesh ( Deuteronomy 1:19-23 ) is meant, whether-- 
 
    turned--be for turning back, or to denote repetition of offense.

title: Psalms 78:43
text: 43. wrought--set or held forth.

title: Psalms 78:45
text: 45. The dog-fly or the mosquito.

title: Psalms 78:46
text:
46. caterpillar--the Hebrew name, from its voracity, and that of-- 
 
    locust--from its multitude.

title: Psalms 78:47
text: 47, 48. The additional effects of the storm here mentioned (compare  Exodus 9:23-34 ) are consistent with Moses' account.

title: Psalms 78:48
text: 48. gave ... cattle--literally, "shut up" (compare  Psalms 31:8 ).

title: Psalms 78:49
text: 49. evil angels--or, "angels of evil"--many were perhaps employed, and other evils inflicted.

title: Psalms 78:50
text: 50, 51. made a way--removed obstacles, gave it full scope.

title: Psalms 78:51
text:
51. chief of their strength--literally, "first-fruits," or, "first-born" ( Genesis 49:3 Deuteronomy 21:17 ). 
 
    Ham--one of whose sons gave name (Mizraim, Hebrew) to Egypt.

title: Psalms 78:52
text: 52-54. made his ... forth--or, brought them by periodical journeys (compare  Exodus 15:1 ).

title: Psalms 78:54
text:
54. border of his sanctuary--or, "holy border"-- 
 
    this mountain--(Zion) was, as the seat of civil and religious government, the representative, used for the whole land, as afterwards for the Church ( Isaiah 25:6 Isaiah 25:7 ). 
 
    purchased--or, "procured by His right hand" or power ( Psalms 60:5 ).

title: Psalms 78:55
text:
55. by line--or, the portion thus measured. 
 
    divided them--that is, the heathen, put for their possessions, so tents--that is, of the heathen (compare  Deuteronomy 6:11 ).

title: Psalms 78:56
text: 56, 57. a deceitful bow--which turns back, and so fails to project the arrow ( II Samuel 1:22 Hosea 7:16 ). They relapsed.

title: Psalms 78:58
text: 58. Idolatry resulted from sparing the heathen (compare  Psalms 78:9-11 ).

title: Psalms 78:59
text:
59, 60. heard--perceived ( Genesis 11:7 ). 
 
    abhorred--but not utterly.

title: Psalms 78:60
text: 60. tent ... placed--literally, "caused to dwell," set up ( Joshua 18:1 ).

title: Psalms 78:61
text: 61. his strength--the ark, as symbolical of it ( Psalms 96:6 ).

title: Psalms 78:62
text:
62. gave--or, "shut up." 
 
    his people-- ( Psalms 78:48 I Samuel 4:10-17 ).

title: Psalms 78:63
text:
63. fire--either figure of the slaughter ( I Samuel 4:10 ), or a literal burning by the heathen. 
 
    given to marriage--literally, "praised"--that is, as brides.

title: Psalms 78:64
text:
64. (Compare  I Samuel 4:17 ); and there were, doubtless, others. 
 
    made no lamentation--either because stupefied by grief, or hindered by the enemy.

title: Psalms 78:65
text: 65. (Compare  Psalms 22:16 Isaiah 42:13 ).

title: Psalms 78:66
text: 66. And he smote ... part--or, "struck His enemies' back." The Philistines never regained their position after their defeats by David.

title: Psalms 78:67
text:
67, 68. tabernacle of Joseph--or, "home," or, "tribe," to which-- 
 
    tribe of Ephraim--is parallel (compare  Revelation of John 7:8 ). Its pre-eminence was, like Saul's, only permitted. Judah had been the choice ( Genesis 49:10 ).

title: Psalms 78:69
text:
69. Exalted as-- 
 
    high palaces--or, "mountains," and abiding as--the earth.

title: Psalms 78:70
text: 70-72. God's sovereignty was illustrated in this choice. The contrast is striking--humility and exaltation--and the correspondence is beautiful.

title: Psalms 78:71
text: 71. following ... ewes, &c.--literally, "ewes giving suck" (compare  Isaiah 40:11 ). On the pastoral terms, compare  Psalms 79:13 .

title: Psalms 79:1
text:
Psalms 79:1-13 . This Psalm, like the seventy-fourth, probably depicts the desolations of the Chaldeans ( Jeremiah 52:12-24 ). It comprises the usual complaint, prayer, and promised thanks for relief. 
 
    1. (Compare  Psalms 74:2-7 ).

title: Psalms 79:2
text: 2, 3. (Compare  Jeremiah 15:3 Jeremiah 16:4 ).

title: Psalms 79:4
text: 4. (Compare  Psalms 44:13 Jeremiah 42:18 Lamentations 2:15 ).

title: Psalms 79:5
text:
5. How long-- ( Psalms 13:1 ). 
 
    be angry-- ( Psalms 74:1-10 ). 
 
    jealousy burn-- ( Deuteronomy 29:20 ).

title: Psalms 79:6
text:
6, 7. (Compare  Jeremiah 10:25 ). Though we deserve much, do not the heathen deserve more for their violence to us ( Jeremiah 51:3-5 Zechariah 1:14 )? The singular denotes the chief power, and the use of the plural indicates the combined confederates. 
 
    called upon--or, "by" 
 
    thy name--proclaimed Thy attributes and professed allegiance ( Isaiah 12:4 Acts 2:21 ).

title: Psalms 79:8
text:
8. former iniquities--literally, "iniquities of former times." 
 
    prevent us--literally, "meet us," as in  Psalms 21:3 .

title: Psalms 79:9
text:
9. for ... glory of thy name [and for] thy name's sake--both mean for illustrating Thy attributes, faithfulness, power, &c. 
 
    purge ... sins--literally, "provide atonement for us." Deliverance from sin and suffering, for their good and God's glory, often distinguish the prayers of Old Testament saints (compare  Ephesians 1:7 ).

title: Psalms 79:10
text:
10. This ground of pleading often used ( Exodus 32:12 Numbers 14:13-16 ). 
 
    blood ... shed-- ( Psalms 79:3 ).

title: Psalms 79:11
text:
11. prisoner--the whole captive people. 
 
    power--literally, "arm" ( Psalms 10:15 ).

title: Psalms 79:12
text: 12. into their bosom--The lap or folds of the dress is used by Eastern people for receiving articles. The figure denotes retaliation (compare  Isaiah 65:6 Isaiah 65:7 ). They reproached God as well as His people.

title: Psalms 79:13
text: 13. sheep ... pasture--(Compare  Psalms 74:1 Psalms 78:70 ).

title: Psalms 80:1
text:
Psalms 80:1-19 . Shoshannim--"Lilies" (see on  Psalms 44:26 , title).  Eduth--Testimony, referring to the topic as a testimony of God to His people (compare  Psalms 19:7 ). This Psalm probably relates to the captivity of the ten tribes, as the former to that of Judah. Its complaint is aggravated by the contrast of former prosperity, and the prayer for relief occurs as a refrain through the Psalm. 
 
    1, 2. Joseph--for Ephraim ( I Chronicles 7:20-29 Psalms 78:67 Revelation of John 7:8 ), for Israel. 
 
    Shepherd--(Compare  Genesis 49:24 ). 
 
    leadest, &c.-- ( Psalms 77:20 ). 
 
    dwellest ... cherubim-- ( Exodus 25:20 ); the place of God's visible glory, whence He communed with the people ( Hebrews 9:5 ). 
 
    shine forth--appear ( Psalms 50:2 Psalms 94:1 ).

title: Psalms 80:2
text: 2. Before Ephraim, &c.--These tribes marched next the ark ( Numbers 2:18-24 ). The name of Benjamin may be introduced merely in allusion to that fact, and not because that tribe was identified with Israel in the schism ( I Kings 12:16-21 ; compare also  Numbers 10:24 ).

title: Psalms 80:3
text:
3. Turn us--that is, from captivity. 
 
    thy face to shine-- ( Numbers 6:25 ).

title: Psalms 80:4
text: 4. be angry--(Compare Margin.)

title: Psalms 80:5
text: 5. bread of tears--still an Eastern figure for affliction.

title: Psalms 80:6
text: 6. strife--object or cause of ( Isaiah 9:11 ). On last clause compare  Psalms 79:4 Ezekiel 36:4 .

title: Psalms 80:8
text:
8-11. brought--or, "plucked up," as by roots, to be replanted. 
 
    a vine-- ( Psalms 78:47 ). The figure ( Isaiah 16:8 ) represents the flourishing state of Israel, as predicted ( Genesis 28:14 ), and verified ( I Kings 4:20-25 ).

title: Psalms 80:12
text: 12. hedges-- ( Isaiah 5:5 ).

title: Psalms 80:13
text:
13. The boar--may represent the ravaging Assyrian and 
 
    the wild beast--other heathen.

title: Psalms 80:14
text: 14, 15. visit this vine--favorably ( Psalms 8:4 ).

title: Psalms 80:15
text:
15. And the vineyard--or, "And protect or guard what thy right hand," &c. 
 
    the branch--literally, "over the Son of man," preceding this phrase, with "protect" or "watch." 
 
    for thyself--a tacit allusion to the plea for help; for

title: Psalms 80:16
text:
16. it--the "vine" or 
 
    they--the "people" are suffering from Thy displeasure.

title: Psalms 80:17
text:
17. thy hand ... upon--that is, strengthen ( Ezra 7:6 Ezra 8:22 ). 
 
    man of ... hand--may allude to Benjamin ( Genesis 35:18 ). The terms in the latter clause correspond with those of  Psalms 80:15 , from "and the branch," &c., literally, and confirm the exposition given above.

title: Psalms 80:18
text: 18. We need quickening grace ( Psalms 71:20 Psalms 119:25 ) to persevere in Thy right worship ( Genesis 4:26 Romans 10:11 ).

title: Psalms 80:19
text: 19. (Compare  Psalms 80:3 , "O God";  Psalms 80:7 , "O God of hosts").

title: Psalms 81:1
text:
Psalms 81:1-16 . Gittith--(See on  Psalms 7:17 , title). A festal Psalm, probably for the passover (compare  Matthew 26:30 ), in which, after an exhortation to praise God, He is introduced, reminding Israel of their obligations, chiding their neglect, and depicting the happy results of obedience. 
 
    1. our strength-- ( Psalms 38:7 ).

title: Psalms 81:2
text: 2. unites the most joyful kinds of music, vocal and instrumental.

title: Psalms 81:3
text:
3. the new moon--or the month. 
 
    the time appointed--(Compare  Proverbs 7:20 ).

title: Psalms 81:5
text:
5. a testimony--The feasts, especially the passover, attested God's relation to His people. 
 
    Joseph--for Israel ( Psalms 80:1 ). 
 
    went out through--or, "over," that is, Israel in the exodus. 
 
    I heard--change of person. The writer speaks for the nation. 
 
    language--literally, "lip" ( Psalms 14:1 ). An aggravation or element of their distress that their oppressors were foreigners ( Deuteronomy 28:49 ).

title: Psalms 81:6
text: 6. God's language alludes to the burdensome slavery of the Israelites.

title: Psalms 81:7
text:
7. secret place--the cloud from which He troubled the Egyptians ( Exodus 14:24 ). 
 
    proved thee-- ( Psalms 7:10 Psalms 17:3 ) --tested their faith by the miracle.

title: Psalms 81:8
text:
8. (Compare  Psalms 50:7 ). The reproof follows to  Psalms 81:12 . 
 
    if thou wilt hearken--He then propounds the terms of His covenant: they should worship Him alone, who ( Psalms 81:10 ) had delivered them, and would still confer all needed blessings.

title: Psalms 81:11
text: 11, 12. They failed, and He gave them up to their own desires and hardness of heart ( Deuteronomy 29:18 Proverbs 1:30 Romans 11:25 ).

title: Psalms 81:13
text: 13-16. Obedience would have secured all promised blessings and the subjection of foes. In this passage, "should have," "would have," &c., are better, "should" and "would" expressing God's intention at the time, that is, when they left Egypt.

title: Psalms 82:1
text:
Psalms 82:1-8 . Before the great Judge, the judges of the earth are rebuked, exhorted, and threatened. 
 
    1. congregation--(Compare  Exodus 12:3 Exodus 16:1 ). 
 
    of the mighty--that is, of God, of His appointment. 
 
    the gods--or, "judges" ( Exodus 21:6 Exodus 22:9 ), God's representatives.

title: Psalms 82:2
text: 2. accept the persons--literally, "lift up the faces," that is, from dejection, or admit to favor and communion, regardless of merit ( Leviticus 19:15 Proverbs 18:5 ).

title: Psalms 82:3
text: 3, 4. So must good judges act ( Psalms 10:14 Job 29:12 ).

title: Psalms 82:4
text: 4. poor and needy--(Compare  Psalms 34:10 Psalms 41:1 ).

title: Psalms 82:5
text:
5. By the wilful ignorance and negligence of judges, anarchy ensues ( Psalms 11:3 Psalms 75:3 ). 
 
    out of course--(Compare Margin;  Psalms 9:6 Psalms 62:2 ).

title: Psalms 82:6
text: 6, 7. Though God admitted their official dignity ( John 10:34 ), He reminds them of their mortality.

title: Psalms 82:7
text: 7. fall like, &c.--be cut off suddenly ( Psalms 20:8 Psalms 91:7 ).

title: Psalms 82:8
text: 8. As rightful sovereign of earth, God is invoked personally to correct the evils of His representatives.

title: Psalms 83:1
text:
Psalms 83:1-18 . Of Asaph--(See on  Psalms 73:28 , title). The historical occasion is probably that of  II Chronicles 20:1 II Chronicles 20:2  (compare  Psalms 47:1-9 Psalms 48:1-14 ). After a general petition, the craft and rage of the combined enemies are described, God's former dealings recited, and a like summary and speedy destruction on them is invoked. 
 
    1. God addressed as indifferent (compare  Psalms 35:22 Psalms 39:12 ). 
 
    be not still--literally, "not quiet," as opposed to action.

title: Psalms 83:2
text: 2. thine enemies--as well as ours ( Psalms 74:23 Isaiah 37:23 ).

title: Psalms 83:3
text: 3. hidden ones--whom God specially protects ( Psalms 27:5 Psalms 91:1 ).

title: Psalms 83:4
text:
4. from being a nation--utter destruction ( Isaiah 7:8 Isaiah 23:1 ). 
 
    Israel--here used for Judah, having been the common name.

title: Psalms 83:5
text:
5. they have consulted--with heart, or cordially. 
 
    together--all alike.

title: Psalms 83:6
text:
6-8. tabernacles--for people ( Psalms 78:67 ). 
 
    they--all these united with the children of Lot, or Ammonites and Moabites (compare  II Chronicles 20:1 ).

title: Psalms 83:9
text: 9-11. Compare the similar fate of these ( II Chronicles 20:23 ) with that of the foes mentioned in  Judges 7:22 , here referred to. They destroyed one another ( Judges 4:6-24 Judges 7:25 ). Human remains form manure (compare  II Kings 9:37 Jeremiah 9:22 ).

title: Psalms 83:12
text:
12. The language of the invaders. 
 
    houses--literally, "residences," enclosures, as for flocks ( Psalms 65:12 ). 
 
    of God--as the proprietors of the land ( II Chronicles 20:11 Isaiah 14:25 ).

title: Psalms 83:13
text: 13. like a wheel--or, whirling of any light thing ( Isaiah 17:13 ), as stubble or chaff ( Psalms 1:4 ).

title: Psalms 83:14
text: 14, 15. Pursue them to an utter destruction.

title: Psalms 83:16
text: 16. that they may seek--or as  Psalms 83:18 , supply "men," since  Psalms 83:17 Psalms 83:18  amplify the sentiment of  Psalms 83:16 , expressing more fully the measure of destruction, and the lesson of God's being and perfections (compare  II Chronicles 20:29 ) taught to all men.

title: Psalms 84:1
text:
Psalms 84:1-12 . (See on  Psalms 7:17 , title, and  Psalms 41:13 , title).  The writer describes the desirableness of God's worship and prays for a restoration to its privileges. 
 
    1. amiable--not lovely, but beloved. 
 
    tabernacles-- ( Psalms 43:3 ).

title: Psalms 84:2
text:
2. longeth--most intensely ( Genesis 31:30 Psalms 17:12 ). 
 
    fainteth--exhausted with desire. 
 
    courts--as tabernacles ( Psalms 84:1 ) --the whole building. 
 
    crieth out--literally, "sings for joy"; but here, and  Lamentations 2:19 , expresses an act of sorrow as the corresponding noun ( Psalms 17:1 Psalms 61:2 ). 
 
    heart and ... flesh--as in  Psalms 63:1 .

title: Psalms 84:3
text: 3. thine altars--that is, of burnt offering and incense, used for the whole tabernacle. Its structure afforded facilities for sparrows and swallows to indulge their known predilections for such places. Some understand the statement as to the birds as a comparison: "as they find homes, so do I desire thine altars," &c.

title: Psalms 84:4
text: 4. This view is favored by the language here, which, as in  Psalms 15:1 Psalms 23:6 , recognizes the blessing of membership in God's family by terms denoting a dwelling in His house.

title: Psalms 84:5
text:
5. (Compare  Psalms 68:28 ). 
 
    in whose heart ... the ways--that is, who knows and loves the way to God's favor ( Proverbs 16:17 Isaiah 40:3 Isaiah 40:4 ).

title: Psalms 84:6
text: 6. valley of Baca--or, "weeping." Through such, by reason of their dry and barren condition, the worshippers often had to pass to Jerusalem. As they might become wells, or fountains, or pools, supplied by refreshing rain, so the grace of God, by the exercises of His worship, refreshes and revives the hearts of His people, so that for sorrows they have "rivers of delight" ( Psalms 36:8 Psalms 46:4 ).

title: Psalms 84:7
text:
7. The figure of the pilgrim is carried out. As such daily refit their bodily strength till they reach Jerusalem, so the spiritual worshipper is daily supplied with spiritual strength by God's grace till he appears before God in heaven. 
 
    appeareth ... God--the terms of the requisition for the attendance on the feasts (compare  Deuteronomy 16:16 ),

title: Psalms 84:9
text:
9. God is addressed as a shield (compare  Psalms 84:11 ). 
 
    thine anointed--David ( I Samuel 16:12 ).

title: Psalms 84:10
text: 10. I had ... doorkeeper--literally, "I choose to sit on the threshold," the meanest place.

title: Psalms 84:11
text:
11, 12. As a sun God enlightens ( Psalms 27:1 ); as a shield He protects. 
 
    grace--God's favor, its fruit-- 
 
    glory--the honor He bestows. 
 
    uprightly-- ( Psalms 15:2 Psalms 18:23 ).

title: Psalms 84:12
text: 12. that trusteth--constantly.

title: Psalms 85:1
text:
Psalms 85:1-13 . On the ground of former mercies, the Psalmist prays for renewed blessings, and, confidently expecting them, rejoices. 
 
    1. captivity--not necessarily the Babylonian, but any great evil ( Psalms 14:7 ).

title: Psalms 85:2
text: 2, 3. (Compare  Psalms 32:1-5 ).

title: Psalms 85:3
text: 3. To turn from the "fierceness," implies that He was reconcilable, though

title: Psalms 85:4
text: 4-7. having still occasion for the anger which is deprecated.

title: Psalms 85:5
text: 5. draw out--or, "prolong" ( Psalms 36:10 ).

title: Psalms 85:8
text:
8. He is confident God will favor His penitent people ( Psalms 51:17 Psalms 80:18 ). 
 
    saints--as in  Psalms 4:3 , the "godly."

title: Psalms 85:9
text: 9. They are here termed "them that fear him"; and grace produces glory ( Psalms 84:11 ).

title: Psalms 85:10
text: 10. God's promises of "mercy" will be verified by His "truth" (compare  Psalms 25:10 Psalms 40:10 ); and the "work of righteousness" in His holy government shall be "peace" ( Isaiah 32:17 ). There is an implied contrast with a dispensation under which God's truth sustains His threatened wrath, and His righteousness inflicts misery on the wicked.

title: Psalms 85:11
text: 11. Earth and heaven shall abound with the blessings of this government;

title: Psalms 85:12
text: 12, 13. and, under this, the deserted land shall be productive, and men be "set," or guided in God's holy ways. Doubtless, in this description of God's returning favor, the writer had in view that more glorious period, when Christ shall establish His government on God's reconciled justice and abounding mercy.

title: Psalms 86:1
text:
Psalms 86:1-17 . This is a prayer in which the writer, with deep emotion, mingles petitions and praises, now urgent for help, and now elated with hope, in view of former mercies. The occurrence of many terms and phrases peculiar to David's Psalms clearly intimates its authorship. 
 
    1, 2. poor and needy--a suffering child of God, as in  Psalms 10:12 Psalms 10:17 Psalms 18:27 . 
 
    I am holy--or, "godly," as in  Psalms 4:3 Psalms 85:8 .

title: Psalms 86:4
text: 4. lift up my soul--with strong desire ( Psalms 25:1 ).

title: Psalms 86:5
text: 5-7. unto all ... that call upon thee--or, "worship Thee" ( Psalms 50:15 Psalms 91:15 ) however undeserving ( Exodus 34:6 Leviticus 11:9-13 ).

title: Psalms 86:8
text: 8. neither ... works--literally, "nothing like thy works," the "gods" have none at all.

title: Psalms 86:9
text: 9, 10. The pious Jews believed that God's common relation to all would be ultimately acknowledged by all men ( Psalms 45:12-16 Psalms 47:9 ).

title: Psalms 86:11
text:
11. Teach--Show, point out. 
 
    the way--of Providence. 
 
    walk in thy truth--according to its declarations. 
 
    unite my heart--fix all my affections ( Psalms 12:2 James 4:8 ). 
 
    to fear thy name--(compare  Psalms 86:12 ) to honor Thy perfections.

title: Psalms 86:13
text: 13, 14. The reason: God had delivered him from death and the power of insolent, violent, and godless persecutors ( Psalms 54:3 Ezekiel 8:12 ).

title: Psalms 86:15
text: 15. Contrasts God with his enemies (compare  Psalms 86:5 ).

title: Psalms 86:16
text: 16. son ... handmaid--homeborn servant (compare  Luke 15:17 ).

title: Psalms 86:17
text: 17. Show me--literally, "Make with me a token," by Thy providential care. Thus in and by his prosperity his enemies would be confounded.

title: Psalms 87:1
text:
Psalms 87:1-7 . This triumphal song was probably occasioned by the same event as the forty-sixth [see on  Psalms 45:17 , title]. The writer celebrates the glory of the Church, as the means of spiritual blessing to the nation. 
 
    1. His--that is, God's 
 
    foundation--or, what He has founded, that is, Zion ( Isaiah 14:32 ). 
 
    is in the holy mountains--the location of Zion, in the wide sense, for the capital, or Jerusalem, being on several hills.

title: Psalms 87:2
text: 2. gates--for the enclosures, or city to which they opened ( Psalms 9:14 Psalms 122:2 ; compare  Psalms 132:13 Psalms 132:14 ).

title: Psalms 87:3
text: 3. spoken of thee--or, "in thee," that is, the city of God ( Psalms 46:4 Psalms 48:2 ).

title: Psalms 87:4
text:
4. This is what is spoken by God. 
 
    to them ... me--literally, "for My knowers," they are true worshippers ( Psalms 36:10 Isaiah 19:21 ). These are mentioned as specimens. 
 
    this--that is, nation 
 
    was born there--Of each it is said, "This was born," or is a native of Zion, spiritually.

title: Psalms 87:5
text:
5. The writer resumes-- 
 
    This and that man--literally, "man and man," or many ( Genesis 14:10 Exodus 8:10 Exodus 8:14 ), or all ( Isaiah 44:5 Galatians 3:28 ). 
 
    the highest ... her--God is her protector.|

title: Psalms 87:6
text: 6. The same idea is set forth under the figure of a register made by God (compare  Isaiah 4:3 ).

title: Psalms 87:7
text:
7. As in a great procession of those thus written up, or registered, seeking Zion ( Isaiah 2:3 Jeremiah 50:5 ), "the singers" and "players," or pipers, shall precede. 
 
    all my springs--So each shall say, "All my sources of spiritual joy are in Thee" ( Psalms 46:4 Psalms 84:6 ).

title: Psalms 88:1
text:
Psalms 88:1-18 . Upon Mahalath--either an instrument, as a lute, to be used as an accompaniment (Leannoth, "for singing") or, as others think, an enigmatic title (see on  Psalms 4:8 ,  Psalms 21:13 , and  Psalms 44:26 , titles), denoting the subject--that is, "sickness or disease, for humbling," the idea of spiritual maladies being often represented by disease (compare  Psalms 6:5 Psalms 6:6 Psalms 22:14 Psalms 22:15 , &c.). On the other terms, see on  Psalms 41:13  and  Psalms 31:24 . Heman and Ethan (see on  Psalms 88:18 , title) were David's singers ( I Chronicles 6:18 I Chronicles 6:33 I Chronicles 15:17 ), of the family of Kohath. If the persons alluded to ( I Kings 4:31 I Chronicles 2:6 ), they were probably adopted into the tribe of Judah. Though called a song, which usually implies joy ( Psalms 83:1 ), both the style and matter of the Psalm are very despondent; yet the appeals to God evince faith, and we may suppose that the word "song" might be extended to such compositions. 
 
    1, 2. Compare on the terms used,  Psalms 22:2 Psalms 31:2 .

title: Psalms 88:3
text: 3. grave--literally, "hell" ( Psalms 16:10 ), death in wide sense.

title: Psalms 88:4
text:
4. go ... pit--of destruction ( Psalms 28:1 ). 
 
    as a man--literally, "a stout man," whose strength is utterly gone.

title: Psalms 88:5
text: 5. Free ... dead--Cut off from God's care, as are the slain, who, falling under His wrath, are left, no longer sustained by His hand.

title: Psalms 88:6
text: 6. Similar figures for distress in  Psalms 63:9 Psalms 69:3 .

title: Psalms 88:7
text: 7. Compare  Psalms 38:2 , on first, and  Psalms 42:7 , on last clause.

title: Psalms 88:8
text: 8. Both cut off from sympathy and made hateful to friends ( Psalms 31:11 ).

title: Psalms 88:9
text:
9. Mine eye mourneth--literally, "decays," or fails, denoting exhaustion ( Psalms 6:7 Psalms 31:9 ). 
 
    I ... called-- ( Psalms 86:5 Psalms 86:7 ). 
 
    stretched out--for help ( Psalms 44:20 ).

title: Psalms 88:10
text:
10. shall the dead--the remains of ghosts. 
 
    arise--literally, "rise up," that is, as dead persons.

title: Psalms 88:11
text: 11, 12. amplify the foregoing, the whole purport (as  Psalms 6:5 ) being to contrast death and life as seasons for praising God.

title: Psalms 88:13
text: 13. prevent--meet--that is, he will diligently come before God for help ( Psalms 18:41 ).

title: Psalms 88:14
text: 14. On the terms ( Psalms 27:9 Psalms 74:1 Psalms 77:7 ).

title: Psalms 88:15
text: 15. from ... youth up--all my life.

title: Psalms 88:16
text: 16, 17. the extremes of anguish and despair are depicted.

title: Psalms 88:18
text: 18. into darkness--Better omit "into"--"mine acquaintances (are) darkness," the gloom of death, &c. ( Job 17:13 Job 17:14 ).

title: Psalms 89:1
text:
Psalms 89:1-52 . Of Ethan--(See on  Psalms 87:7 , title). This Psalm was composed during some season of great national distress, perhaps Absalom's rebellion. It contrasts the promised prosperity and perpetuity of David's throne (with reference to the great promise of  II Samuel 7:12-17 ), with a time when God appeared to have forgotten His covenant. The picture thus drawn may typify the promises and the adversities of Christ's kingdom, and the terms of confiding appeal to God provided appropriate prayers for the divine aid and promised blessing. 
 
    1. mercies--those promised ( Isaiah 55:3 Acts 13:34 ), and-- 
 
    faithfulness--that is, in fulfilling them.

title: Psalms 89:2
text: 2. I have said--expressed, as well as felt, my convictions ( II Corinthians 4:13 ).

title: Psalms 89:3
text:
3, 4. The object of this faith expressed in God's words ( II Samuel 7:11-16 ). 
 
    with--or literally, "to" 
 
    my chosen--as the covenant is in the form of a promise.

title: Psalms 89:6
text:
6, 7. This is worthy of our belief, for His faithfulness (is praised) by the congregation of saints or holy ones; that is, angels (compare  Deuteronomy 33:2 Daniel 8:13 ). 
 
    sons of the mighty--(compare  Psalms 29:1 ). So is He to be admired on earth.

title: Psalms 89:8
text: 8-14. To illustrate His power and faithfulness examples are cited from history. His control of the sea (the most mighty and unstable object in nature), and of Egypt ( Psalms 87:4 ), the first great foe of Israel (subjected to utter helplessness from pride and insolence), are specimens. At the same time, the whole frame of nature founded and sustained by Him, Tabor and Hermon for "east and west," and "north and south," together representing the whole world, declare the same truth as to His attributes.

title: Psalms 89:12
text: 12. rejoice in thy name--praise Thy perfections by their very existence.

title: Psalms 89:15
text:
15. His government of righteousness is served by "mercy" and "truth" as ministers ( Psalms 85:10-13 ). 
 
    know the joyful sound--understand and appreciate the spiritual blessings symbolized by the feasts to which the people were called by the trumpet ( Leviticus 25:9 , &c.). 
 
    walk ... countenance--live in His favor ( Psalms 4:6 Psalms 44:3 ).

title: Psalms 89:16
text:
16, 17. in--or, "by" 
 
    thy righteousness--Thy faithful just rule. 
 
    glory--or, "beauty." 
 
    of their strength--They shall be adorned as well as protected. 
 
    our horn--exalt our power ( Psalms 75:10 Luke 1:69 ).

title: Psalms 89:18
text: 18. (Margin). Thus is introduced the promise to "our shield," "our king," David.

title: Psalms 89:19
text:
19-37. Then--when the covenant was established, of whose execution the exalted views of God now given furnish assurance. 
 
    thou ... to thy holy one--or godly saint, object of favor ( Psalms 4:3 ). Nathan is meant ( II Samuel 7:17 I Chronicles 17:3-15 ). 
 
    laid help--literally, "given help." David was chosen and then exalted.

title: Psalms 89:20
text: 20. I have found--having sought and then selected him ( I Samuel 16:1-6 ).

title: Psalms 89:21
text: 21. will protect and sustain ( Isaiah 41:10 ),

title: Psalms 89:22
text: 22-25. by restraining and conquering his enemies, and performing My gracious purpose of extending his dominion--

title: Psalms 89:25
text:
25. hand [and] right hand--power ( Psalms 17:7 Psalms 60:5 ). 
 
    sea, and ... rivers--limits of his empire ( Psalms 72:8 ).

title: Psalms 89:26
text: 26, 27. first-born--one who is chief, most beloved or distinguished ( Exodus 4:22 Colossians 1:15 ). In God's sight and purposes he was the first among all monarchs, and specially so in his typical relation to Christ.

title: Psalms 89:28
text: 28-37. This relation is perpetual with David's descendants, as a whole typical in official position of his last greatest descendant. Hence though in personal relations any of them might be faithless and so punished, their typical relation shall continue. His oath confirms His promise, and the most enduring objects of earth and heaven illustrate its perpetual force ( Psalms 72:5 Psalms 72:7 Psalms 72:17 ).

title: Psalms 89:35
text:
35. Once--one thing ( Psalms 27:4 ). 
 
    by my holiness--as a holy God. 
 
    that I will not lie--literally, "if I lie"--part of the form of swearing ( I Samuel 24:6 II Samuel 3:35 ).

title: Psalms 89:37
text: 37. It shall ... moon ... heaven--literally, "As the moon, and the witness in the sky is sure, that is, the moon."

title: Psalms 89:38
text:
38-52. present a striking contrast to these glowing promises, in mournful evidences of a loss of God's favor. 
 
    cast off--and rejected (compare  Psalms 15:4 Psalms 43:2 Psalms 44:9 ).

title: Psalms 89:39
text: 39. An insult to the "crown," as of divine origin, was a profanation.

title: Psalms 89:40
text: 40-45. The ruin is depicted under several figures--a vineyard whose broken "hedges," and "strongholds," whose ruins invite spoilers and invaders; a warrior, whose enemies are aided by God, and whose sword's "edge"--literally, "rock" or "strength" ( Joshua 5:2 ) is useless; and a youth prematurely old.

title: Psalms 89:45
text: 45. days of his youth--or, "youthful vigor," that is, of the royal line, or promised perpetual kingdom, under the figure of a man.

title: Psalms 89:46
text: 46. How long, &c.--(Compare  Psalms 13:1 Psalms 88:14 Jeremiah 4:4 ).

title: Psalms 89:47
text: 47. These expostulations are excited in view of the identity of the prosperity of this kingdom with the welfare of all mankind ( Genesis 22:18 Psalms 72:17 Isaiah 9:7 Isaiah 11:1-10 ); for if such is the fate of this chosen royal line.

title: Psalms 89:48
text: 48. What man--literally, "strong man--shall live?" and, indeed, have not all men been made in vain, as to glorifying God?

title: Psalms 89:49
text: 49-51. The terms of expostulation are used in view of the actual appearance that God had forsaken His people and forgotten His promise, and the plea for aid is urged in view of the reproaches of His and His people's enemies (compare  Isaiah 37:17-35 ).

title: Psalms 89:50
text:
50. bear in my bosom--as feeling the affliction of the people ( Psalms 69:9 ). 
 
    footsteps--ways ( Psalms 56:6 ).

title: Psalms 89:52
text:
52. Blessed, &c.--denotes returning confidence ( Psalms 34:1-3 ). 
 
    Amen, and Amen--closes the third book of Psalms.

title: Psalms 90:1
text:
Psalms 90:1-17 . Contrasting man's frailty with God's eternity, the writer mourns over it as the punishment of sin, and prays for a return of the divine favor. A Prayer [mainly such] of Moses the man of God-- ( Deuteronomy 33:1 Joshua 14:6 ); as such he wrote this (see on  Psalms 17:15 , title, and  Psalms 35:28 , title). 
 
    1. dwelling-place--home (compare  Ezekiel 11:16 ), as a refuge ( Deuteronomy 33:27 ).

title: Psalms 90:2
text: 2. brought forth [and] formed--both express the idea of production by birth.

title: Psalms 90:3
text: 3. to destruction--literally, "even to dust" ( Genesis 3:19 ), which is partly quoted in the last clause.

title: Psalms 90:4
text:
4. Even were our days now a thousand years, as Adam's, our life would be but a moment in God's sight ( II Peter 3:8 ). 
 
    a watch--or, third part of a night (compare  Exodus 14:24 ).

title: Psalms 90:5
text: 5, 6. Life is like grass, which, though changing under the influence of the night's dew, and flourishing in the morning, is soon cut down and withereth ( Psalms 103:15 I Peter 1:24 ).

title: Psalms 90:7
text:
7, 8. For--A reason, this is the infliction of God's wrath. 
 
    troubled--literally, "confounded by terror" ( Psalms 2:5 ). Death is by sin ( Romans 5:12 ). Though "secret," the light of God's countenance, as a candle, will bring sin to view ( Proverbs 20:27 I Corinthians 4:5 ).

title: Psalms 90:9
text:
9. are passed--literally, "turn," as to depart ( Jeremiah 6:4 ). 
 
    spend--literally, "consume." 
 
    as a tale--literally, "a thought," or, "a sigh" ( Ezekiel 2:10 ).

title: Psalms 90:10
text:
10. Moses life was an exception ( Deuteronomy 34:7 ). 
 
    it is ... cut off--or, "driven," as is said of the quails in using the same word ( Numbers 11:31 ). In view of this certain and speedy end, life is full of sorrow.

title: Psalms 90:11
text: 11. The whole verse may be read as a question implying the negative, "No one knows what Thy anger can do, and what Thy wrath is, estimated by a true piety."

title: Psalms 90:12
text: 12. This he prays we may know or understand, so as properly to number or appreciate the shortness of our days, that we may be wise.

title: Psalms 90:13
text:
13. (Compare  Psalms 13:2 ). 
 
    let it repent--a strong figure, as in  Exodus 32:12 , imploring a change in His dealings.

title: Psalms 90:14
text: 14. early--promptly.

title: Psalms 90:15
text: 15. As have been our sorrows, so let our joys be great and long.

title: Psalms 90:16
text:
16. thy work--or, providential acts. 
 
    thy glory-- ( Psalms 8:5 Psalms 45:3 ), the honor accruing from Thy work of mercy to us.

title: Psalms 90:17
text: 17. let the beauty--or sum of His gracious acts, in their harmony, be illustrated in us, and favor our enterprise.

title: Psalms 91:1
text:
Psalms 91:1-16 . David is the most probable author; and the pestilence, mentioned in  II Samuel 24:13-15 , the most probable of any special occasion to which the Psalm may refer. The changes of person allowable in poetry are here frequently made. 
 
    1. dwelleth in the secret place-- ( Psalms 27:5 Psalms 31:20 ) denotes nearness to God. Such as do so abide or lodge secure from assaults, and can well use the terms of trust in  Psalms 91:2 .

title: Psalms 91:3
text: 3. snares ... [and] ... noisome pestilence--literally, "plagues of mischiefs" ( Psalms 5:9 Psalms 52:7 ), are expressive figures for various evils.

title: Psalms 91:4
text:
4. For the first figure compare  Deuteronomy 32:11 Matthew 23:37 . 
 
    buckler--literally, "surrounding"--that is, a kind of shield covering all over.

title: Psalms 91:5
text:
5. terror--or, what causes it ( Proverbs 20:2 ). 
 
    by night--then aggravated. 
 
    arrow--that is, of enemies.

title: Psalms 91:7
text: 7, 8. The security is more valuable, as being special, and, therefore, evidently of God; and while ten thousands of the wicked fall, the righteous are in such safety that they only see the calamity.

title: Psalms 91:9
text: 9-12. This exemption from evil is the result of trust in God, who employs angels as ministering spirits ( Hebrews 1:14 ).

title: Psalms 91:13
text: 13. Even the fiercest, strongest, and most insidious animals may be trampled on with impunity.

title: Psalms 91:14
text:
14-16. God Himself speaks (compare  Psalms 46:10 Psalms 75:2 Psalms 75:3 ). All the terms to express safety and peace indicate the most undoubting confidence (compare  Psalms 18:2 Psalms 20:1 Psalms 22:5 ). 
 
    set his love--that of the most ardent kind.

title: Psalms 91:16
text: 16. show him--literally, "make him see" ( Psalms 50:23 Luke 2:30 ).

title: Psalms 92:1
text:
Psalms 92:1-15 . A Psalm-song--(see on  Psalms 29:11 , title). The theme: God should be praised for His righteous judgments on the wicked and His care and defense of His people. Such a topic, at all times proper, is specially so for the reflections of the Sabbath day. 
 
    1. sing ... name--celebrate Thy perfections.

title: Psalms 92:2
text:
2. in the morning, ... every night--diligently and constantly ( Psalms 42:8 ). 
 
    loving kindness--literally, "mercy." 
 
    faithfulness--in fulfilling promises ( Psalms 89:14 ).

title: Psalms 92:3
text:
3. In such a work all proper aid must be used. 
 
    with a ... sound--or, on Higgaion (see on  Psalms 9:15 ), perhaps an instrument of that name, from its sound resembling the muttered sound of meditation, as expressed also by the word. This is joined with the harp.

title: Psalms 92:4
text: 4. thy work--that is of providence ( Psalms 90:16 Psalms 90:17 ).

title: Psalms 92:5
text: 5. great ... works--correspond to deep or vast thoughts ( Psalms 40:5 Romans 11:23 ).

title: Psalms 92:6
text: 6. A brutish man knoweth not--that is, God's works, so the Psalmist describes himself ( Psalms 73:22 ) when amazed by the prosperity of the wicked, now understood and explained.

title: Psalms 92:8
text:
8. This he does in part, by contrasting their ruin with God's exaltation and eternity. 
 
    most high--as occupying the highest place in heaven ( Psalms 7:7 Psalms 18:16 ).

title: Psalms 92:9
text: 9, 10. A further contrast with the wicked, in the lot of the righteous, safety and triumph.

title: Psalms 92:10
text:
10. horn ... exalt--is to increase power ( Psalms 75:5 ). 
 
    anointed ... fresh--or, "new" 
 
    oil-- ( Psalms 23:5 ) a figure for refreshment (compare  Luke 7:46 ). Such use of oil is still common in the East.

title: Psalms 92:11
text: 11. see ... [and] ... hear my desire--or, literally, "look on" my enemies and hear of the wicked (compare  Psalms 27:11 Psalms 54:7 ) --that is, I shall be gratified by their fall.

title: Psalms 92:12
text: 12-14. The vigorous growth, longevity, utility, fragrance, and beauty of these noble trees, set forth the life, character, and destiny of the pious;

title: Psalms 92:15
text: 15. and they thus declare God's glory as their strong and righteous ruler.

title: Psalms 93:1
text:
Psalms 93:1-5 . This and the six following Psalms were applied by the Jews to the times of the Messiah. The theme is God's supremacy in creation and providence. 
 
    1. God is described as a King entering on His reign, and, for robes of royalty, investing Himself with the glorious attributes of His nature. The result of His thus reigning is the durability of the world.

title: Psalms 93:2
text: 2-4. His underived power exceeds the most sublime exhibitions of the most powerful objects in nature ( Psalms 89:9 ).

title: Psalms 93:5
text: 5. While His power inspires dread, His revealed will should secure our confidence (compare  Psalms 19:7 Psalms 25:10 ), and thus fear and love combined, producing all holy emotions, should distinguish the worship we offer in His house, both earthly and heavenly.

title: Psalms 94:1
text:
Psalms 94:1-23 . The writer, appealing to God in view of the oppression of enemies, rebukes them for their wickedness and folly, and encourages himself, in the confidence that God will punish evildoers, and favor His people. 
 
    1, 2. God's revenge is His judicial infliction of righteous punishment. 
 
    show thyself--(Compare Margin).

title: Psalms 94:2
text: 2. Lift up thyself--or, "Arise," both figures representing God as heretofore indifferent (compare  Psalms 3:7 Psalms 22:16 Psalms 22:20 ).

title: Psalms 94:3
text: 3, 4. In an earnest expostulation he expresses his desire that the insolent triumph of the wicked may be ended.

title: Psalms 94:5
text: 5, 6. thy people [and] thine heritage--are synonymous, the people being often called God's heritage. As justice to the weak is a sign of the best government, their oppression is a sign of the worst ( Deuteronomy 10:18 Isaiah 10:2 ).

title: Psalms 94:7
text: 7. Their cruelty is only exceeded by their wicked and absurd presumption ( Psalms 10:11 Psalms 59:7 ).

title: Psalms 94:8
text: 8. ye brutish--(Compare  Psalms 73:22 Psalms 92:6 ).

title: Psalms 94:9
text: 9-11. The evidence of God's providential government is found in His creative power and omniscience, which also assure us that He can punish the wicked in regard to all their vain purposes.

title: Psalms 94:12
text: 12, 13. On the other hand He favors though He chastens, the pious, and will teach and preserve them till the prosperous wicked are overthrown.

title: Psalms 94:14
text: 14, 15. This results from His abiding love ( Deuteronomy 32:15 ), which is further evinced by His restoring order in His government, whose right administration will be approved by the good.

title: Psalms 94:16
text: 16. These questions imply that none other than God will help ( Psalms 60:9 ),

title: Psalms 94:17
text:
17-19. a fact fully confirmed by his past experience. 
 
    dwelt in silence--as in the grave ( Psalms 31:17 ).

title: Psalms 94:19
text: 19. my thoughts--or, anxious cares.

title: Psalms 94:20
text:
20. throne--power, rulers. 
 
    iniquity [and] mischief--both denote evils done to others, as  Psalms 94:21  explains.

title: Psalms 94:22
text:
22, 23. Yet he is safe in God's care. 
 
    defence-- ( Psalms 59:9 ). 
 
    rock of ... refuge-- ( Psalms 9:9 Psalms 18:2 ).

title: Psalms 94:23
text:
23. bring ... iniquity--(Compare  Psalms 5:10 Psalms 7:16 ). 
 
    in their ... wickedness--while they are engaged in evil doing.

title: Psalms 95:1
text:
Psalms 95:1-11 . David ( Hebrews 4:7 ) exhorts men to praise God for His greatness, and warns them, in God's words, against neglecting His service. 
 
    1. The terms used to express the highest kind of joy. 
 
    rock--a firm basis, giving certainty of salvation ( Psalms 62:7 ).

title: Psalms 95:2
text: 2. come ... presence--literally, "approach," or, meet Him ( Psalms 17:13 ).

title: Psalms 95:3
text: 3. above ... gods--esteemed such by men, though really nothing ( Jeremiah 5:7 Jeremiah 10:10-15 ).

title: Psalms 95:4
text: 4, 5. The terms used describe the world in its whole extent, subject to God.

title: Psalms 95:6
text: 6. come--or, "enter," with solemn forms, as well as hearts.

title: Psalms 95:7
text: 7. This relation illustrates our entire dependence (compare  Psalms 23:3 Psalms 74:1 ). The last clause is united by Paul ( Hebrews 3:7 ) to the following (compare  Psalms 81:8 ),

title: Psalms 95:8
text: 8-11. warning against neglect; and this is sustained by citing the melancholy fate of their rebellious ancestors, whose provoking insolence is described by quoting the language of God's complaint ( Numbers 14:11 ) of their conduct at Meribah and Massah, names given ( Exodus 17:7 ) to commemorate their strife and contention with Him ( Psalms 78:18 Psalms 78:41 ).

title: Psalms 95:10
text:
10. err in their heart--Their wanderings in the desert were but types of their innate ignorance and perverseness. 
 
    that they should not--literally, "if they," &c., part of the form of swearing (compare  Numbers 14:30 Psalms 89:35 ).

title: Psalms 96:1
text:
Psalms 96:1-13 . The substance of this Psalm, and portions of the ninety-seventh, ninety-eighth, and hundredth, are found in  I Chronicles 16:7-36 , which was used by David's directions in the dedication of the tabernacle on Mount Zion. The dispensation of the Messiah was typified by that event, involving, as it did, a more permanent seat of worship, and the introduction of additional and more spiritual services. Hence the language of these Psalms may be regarded as having a higher import than that pertinent to the occasion on which it was thus publicly used. 
 
    1-3. All nations are invited to unite in this most joyful praise. 
 
    new song--literally, "fresh," or new mercies ( Psalms 33:3 Psalms 40:3 ).

title: Psalms 96:2
text:
2. show forth--literally, "declare joyful tidings." 
 
    salvation--illustrates His glory in its wonders of love and mercy.

title: Psalms 96:4
text: 4, 5. For He is not a local God, but of universal agency, while idols are nothing.

title: Psalms 96:6
text: 6. Honour and majesty--are His attendants, declared in His mighty works, while power and grace are specially seen in His spiritual relations to His people.

title: Psalms 96:7
text: 7-9. Give--or, "ascribe" ( Psalms 29:1 ) due honor to Him, by acts of appointed and solemn worship in His house.

title: Psalms 96:8
text: 8. offering--of thanks.

title: Psalms 96:9
text:
9. beauty of holiness-- ( Psalms 29:2 ). 
 
    fear ... him-- ( Psalms 2:11 ).

title: Psalms 96:10
text: 10. Let all know that the government of the world is ordered in justice, and they shall enjoy firm and lasting peace (compare  Psalms 72:3 Psalms 72:7 Isaiah 9:6 Isaiah 9:7 ).

title: Psalms 96:11
text: 11-13. For which reason the universe is invoked to unite in joy, and even inanimate nature ( Romans 8:14-22 ) is poetically represented as capable of joining in the anthem of praise.

title: Psalms 97:1
text:
Psalms 97:1-12 . The writer celebrates the Lord's dominion over nations and nature, describes its effect on foes and friends, and exhorts and encourages the latter. 
 
    1, 2. This dominion is a cause of joy, because, even though our minds are oppressed with terror before the throne of the King of kings ( Exodus 19:16 Deuteronomy 5:22 ), we know it is based on righteous principles and judgments which are according to truth.

title: Psalms 97:3
text: 3-5. The attending illustrations of God's awful justice on enemies ( Psalms 83:14 ) are seen in the disclosures of His almighty power on the elements of nature (compare  Psalms 46:2 Psalms 77:17 Habakkuk 3:6 , &c.).

title: Psalms 97:6
text: 6. heavens--or, their inhabitants ( Psalms 50:6 ), as opposed to "nations" in the latter clause (compare  Isaiah 40:5 Isaiah 66:18 ).

title: Psalms 97:7
text:
7. Idolaters are utterly put to shame, for if angels must worship Him, how much more those who worshipped them. 
 
    all ye gods--literally, "all ye angels" ( Psalms 8:5 Psalms 138:1 Hebrews 1:6 Hebrews 2:7 ). Paul quotes, not as a prophecy, but as language used in regard to the Lord Jehovah, who in the Old Testament theophania is the second person of the Godhead.

title: Psalms 97:8
text:
8, 9. The exaltation of Zion's king is joy to the righteous and sorrow to the wicked. 
 
    daughters of Judah--(Compare  Psalms 48:11 ).

title: Psalms 97:9
text: 9. above all gods-- ( Psalms 95:3 ).

title: Psalms 97:10
text: 10-12. Let gratitude for the blessings of providence and grace incite saints ( Psalms 4:3 ) to holy living. Spiritual blessings are in store, represented by light ( Psalms 27:1 ) and gladness.

title: Psalms 97:11
text: 11. sown--to spring forth abundantly for such, who alone can and well may rejoice in the holy government of their sovereign Lord (compare  Psalms 30:4 Psalms 32:11 ).

title: Psalms 98:1
text:
Psalms 98:1-9 . In view of the wonders of grace and righteousness displayed in God's salvation, the whole creation is invited to unite in praise. 
 
    1. gotten ... victory--literally, "made salvation," enabled Him to save His people. 
 
    right hand, and ... arm--denote power. 
 
    holy arm--or, "arm of holiness," the power of His united moral perfections ( Psalms 22:3 Psalms 32:11 ).

title: Psalms 98:2
text: 2. salvation--the result of His righteousness ( Psalms 7:17 Psalms 31:1 ), and both are publicly displayed.

title: Psalms 98:3
text: 3. The union of mercy and truth ( Psalms 57:3 Psalms 85:10 ) secure the blessings of the promise ( Genesis 12:3 Genesis 18:18 ) to all the world ( Isaiah 52:10 ).

title: Psalms 98:4
text:
4-6. make a loud noise--or, "burst forth" ( Isaiah 14:7 Isaiah 44:23 ). 
 
    before ... King--hail Him as your sovereign; and while, with every aid to demonstrate zeal and joy, intelligent creatures are invited to praise, as in  Psalms 96:11-13 , inanimate nature is also summoned to honor Him who triumphs and rules in righteousness and equity.

title: Psalms 99:1
text:
Psalms 99:1-9 . God's government is especially exercised in and for His Church, which should praise Him for His gracious dealings. 
 
    1. sitteth ... cherubim--(compare  I Samuel 4:4 Psalms 80:1 ). 
 
    tremble ... be moved--inspired with fear by His judgments on the wicked.

title: Psalms 99:2
text: 2. great in Zion--where He dwells ( Psalms 9:11 ).

title: Psalms 99:3
text:
3. thy ... name--perfections of justice, power, &c. 
 
    great and terrible name--producing dread ( Deuteronomy 10:17 ), and to be praised by those over whom He is exalted ( Psalms 97:9 ). 
 
    it is holy--or, "He is holy" ( Psalms 99:5 Psalms 99:9 Isaiah 6:3 ).

title: Psalms 99:4
text:
4, 5. To His wise and righteous government all nations should render honor. 
 
    king's ... judgment--His power is combined with justice. 
 
    he is holy--(compare  Psalms 22:3 ).

title: Psalms 99:6
text:
6-8. The experience of these servants of God is cited for encouragement. 
 
    among ... priests, among ... upon the Lord [and] He spake ... pillar--may be referred to all three (compare  Exodus 18:19 Leviticus 8:15 Deuteronomy 5:5 I Samuel 9:13 ).

title: Psalms 99:7
text: 7. cloudy pillar--the medium of divine intercourse ( Exodus 33:9 Numbers 12:5 ). Obedience was united with worship. God answered them as intercessors for the people, who, though forgiven, were yet chastened ( Exodus 32:10 Exodus 32:34 ).

title: Psalms 100:1
text:
Psalms 100:1-5 . As closing this series (see on  Psalms 92:15 ), this Psalm is a general call on all the earth to render exalted praise to God, the creator, preserver, and benefactor of men. 
 
    1, 2. With thankful praise, unite service as the subjects of a king ( Psalms 2:11 Psalms 2:12 ).

title: Psalms 100:3
text: 3. To the obligations of a creature and subject is added that of a beneficiary ( Psalms 95:7 ).

title: Psalms 100:4
text:
4. Join joyfully in His public worship. The terms are, of course, figurative (compare  Psalms 84:2 Psalms 92:13 Isaiah 66:23 ). 
 
    Enter--or, "Come with solemnity" ( Psalms 95:6 ).

title: Psalms 100:5
text: 5. The reason: God's eternal mercy and truth ( Psalms 25:8 Psalms 89:7 ).

title: Psalms 101:1
text: Psalms 101:1-8 . In this Psalm the profession of the principles of his domestic and political government testifies, as well as actions in accordance with it, David's appreciation of God's mercy to him, and His judgment on his enemies: and thus he sings or celebrates God's dealings.

title: Psalms 101:2
text: 2. He avows his sincere purpose, by God's aid, to act uprightly ( Genesis 17:1 Psalms 18:30 ).

title: Psalms 101:3
text:
3. set ... eyes--as an example to be approved and followed. 
 
    no wicked thing--literally, "word," plan or purpose of Belial ( Psalms 41:8 ). 
 
    work of ... aside--apostates. 
 
    not cleave to me--I will not be implicated in it (compare  Psalms 1:1-3 ).

title: Psalms 101:4
text: 4. A froward heart--or, "perverse heart" ( Psalms 18:26 ). Such a temper I will not indulge, nor even know evil or wickedness.

title: Psalms 101:5
text: 5, 6. The slanderers and haughty persons, so mischievous in society, I will disown; but--

title: Psalms 101:6
text: 6. Mine eyes ... upon--or, I will select reliable and honest men for my servants.

title: Psalms 101:7
text: 7. not dwell--literally, "not sit," or tarry, or be established.

title: Psalms 101:8
text:
8. will early--or, "diligently." 
 
    city of the Lord--or, "holy place" ( Psalms 48:2 ), where wicked men shall not be tolerated.

title: Psalms 102:1
text:
Psalms 102:1-28 . A Prayer of the afflicted, &c.--The general terms seem to denote the propriety of regarding the Psalm as suitably expressive of the anxieties of any one of David's descendants, piously concerned for the welfare of the Church. It was probably David's composition, and, though specially suggested by some peculiar trials, descriptive of future times. overwhelmed--(compare  Psalms 61:2 ). poureth out--pouring out the soul-- ( Psalms 62:8 ). complaint-- ( Psalms 55:2 ). The tone of complaint predominates, though in view of God's promises and abiding faithfulness, it is sometimes exchanged for that of confidence and hope. 
 
    1-3. The terms used occur in  Psalms 4:1 Psalms 17:1 Psalms 17:6 Psalms 18:6 Psalms 31:2 Psalms 31:10 Psalms 37:20 .

title: Psalms 102:4
text:
4. (Compare  Psalms 121:6 ). 
 
    so that I forget--or, "have forgotten," that is, in my distress ( Psalms 107:18 ), and hence strength fails.

title: Psalms 102:5
text: 5. voice ... groaning--effect put for cause, my agony emaciates me.

title: Psalms 102:6
text: 6, 7. The figures express extreme loneliness.

title: Psalms 102:8
text: 8. sworn against me--or literally, "by me," wishing others as miserable as I am ( Numbers 5:21 ).

title: Psalms 102:9
text: 9. ashes--a figure of grief, my bread; weeping or tears, my drink ( Psalms 80:5 ).

title: Psalms 102:10
text: 10. lifted ... cast me down--or, "cast me away" as stubble by a whirlwind ( Isaiah 64:6 ).

title: Psalms 102:11
text: 11. shadow ... declineth--soon to vanish in the darkness of night.

title: Psalms 102:12
text:
12. Contrast with man's frailty (compare  Psalms 90:1-7 ). 
 
    thy remembrance--that by which Thou art remembered, Thy promise.

title: Psalms 102:13
text:
13, 14. Hence it is here adduced. 
 
    for--or, "when." 
 
    the set time, &c.--the time promised, the indication of which is the interest felt for Zion by the people of God.

title: Psalms 102:15
text: 15-17. God's favor to the Church will affect her persecutors with fear.

title: Psalms 102:16
text: 16. When the Lord shall build--or better, "Because the Lord hath built," &c., as a reason for the effect on others; for in thus acting and hearing the humble, He is most glorious.

title: Psalms 102:18
text: 18. people ... created--(compare  Psalms 22:31 ), an organized body, as a Church.

title: Psalms 102:19
text:
19-22. For--or, "That," as introducing the statement of God's condescension. A summary of what shall be written. 
 
    to loose ... appointed--or, "deliver" them ( Psalms 79:11 ).

title: Psalms 102:21
text: 21. To declare, &c.--or, that God's name may be celebrated in the assemblies of His Church, gathered from all nations ( Zechariah 8:20-23 ), and devoted to His service.

title: Psalms 102:23
text:
23-28. The writer, speaking for the Church, finds encouragement in the midst of all his distresses. God's eternal existence is a pledge of faithfulness to His promises. 
 
    in the way--of providence. 
 
    weakened--literally, "afflicted," and made fearful of a premature end, a figure of the apprehensions of the Church, lest God might not perform His promise, drawn from those of a person in view of the dangers of early death (compare  Psalms 89:47 ). Paul ( Hebrews 1:10 ) quotes  Psalms 102:26-28  as addressed to Christ in His divine nature. The scope of the Psalm, as already seen, so far from opposing, favors this view, especially by the sentiments of  Psalms 102:12-15  (compare  Isaiah 60:1 ). The association of the Messiah with a day of future glory to the Church was very intimate in the minds of Old Testament writers; and with correct views of His nature it is very consistent that He should be addressed as the Lord and Head of His Church, who would bring about that glorious future on which they ever dwelt with fond delightful anticipations.

title: Psalms 103:1
text:
Psalms 103:1-22 . A Psalm of joyous praise, in which the writer rises from a thankful acknowledgment of personal blessings to a lively celebration of God's gracious attributes, as not only intrinsically worthy of praise, but as specially suited to man's frailty. He concludes by invoking all creatures to unite in his song. 
 
    1. Bless, &c.--when God is the object, praise. 
 
    my soul--myself ( Psalms 3:3 Psalms 25:1 ), with allusion to the act, as one of intelligence. 
 
    all ... within me-- ( Deuteronomy 6:5 ). 
 
    his holy name-- ( Psalms 5:11 ), His complete moral perfections.

title: Psalms 103:2
text: 2. forget not all--not any, none of His benefits.

title: Psalms 103:3
text: 3. diseases--as penal inflictions ( Deuteronomy 29:22 II Chronicles 21:19 ).

title: Psalms 103:4
text:
4. redeemeth--Cost is implied. 
 
    destruction--literally, "pit of corruption" ( Psalms 16:10 ). 
 
    crowneth--or, "adorneth" ( Psalms 65:11 ). 
 
    tender mercies--compassions (compare  Psalms 25:6 Psalms 40:11 ).

title: Psalms 103:5
text: 5. By God's provision, the saint retains a youthful vigor like the eagles ( Psalms 92:14 ; compare  Isaiah 40:31 ).

title: Psalms 103:6
text: 6. Literally, "righteousness and judgments," denoting various acts of God's government.

title: Psalms 103:7
text:
7. ways--of providence, &c., as usual ( Psalms 25:4 Psalms 67:2 ). 
 
    acts--literally, "wonders" ( Psalms 7:11 Psalms 78:17 ).

title: Psalms 103:8
text:
8-10. God's benevolence implies no merit. He shows it to sinners, who also are chastened for a time ( Exodus 34:6 ). 
 
    keep (anger)--in  Leviticus 19:18 , bear a grudge ( Jeremiah 3:5 Jeremiah 3:12 ).

title: Psalms 103:11
text: 11. great--efficient.

title: Psalms 103:12
text: 12. removed ... from us--so as no longer to affect our relations to Him.

title: Psalms 103:13
text: 13. pitieth--literally, "has compassion on."

title: Psalms 103:14
text:
14. he--"who formed,"  Psalms 94:9 . 
 
    knoweth our frame--literally, "our form." 
 
    we are dust--made of and tending to it ( Genesis 2:7 ).

title: Psalms 103:15
text:
15, 16. So short and frail is life that a breath may destroy it. 
 
    it is gone--literally, "it is not." 
 
    know it no more--no more recognize him ( Psalms 90:6 Isaiah 40:6-8 ).

title: Psalms 103:17
text: 17, 18. For similar contrast compare  Psalms 90:2-6 Psalms 102:27 Psalms 102:28 .

title: Psalms 103:18
text:
18. such ... covenant--limits the general terms preceding. 
 
    righteousness--as usual ( Psalms 7:17 Psalms 31:1 ).

title: Psalms 103:19
text: 19. God's firm and universal dominion is a pledge that He will keep His promises ( Psalms 11:4 Psalms 47:8 ).

title: Psalms 103:20
text: 20-22. do his commandments ... word--or, literally, "so as to hearken," &c., that is, their acts of obedience are prompt, so that they are ever ready to hear, and know, and follow implicitly His declared will (compare  Deuteronomy 26:17 Luke 1:19 ).

title: Psalms 103:21
text: 21. ye his hosts--myriads, or armies, as corresponding to angels of great power ( Psalms 103:20 ), denoting multitudes also.

title: Psalms 103:22
text: 22. all his works--creatures of every sort, everywhere.

title: Psalms 104:1
text:
Psalms 104:1-35 . The Psalmist celebrates God's glory in His works of creation and providence, teaching the dependence of all living creatures; and contrasting the happiness of those who praise Him with the awful end of the wicked. 
 
    1. God's essential glory, and also that displayed by His mighty works, afford ground for praise.

title: Psalms 104:2
text:
2. light--is a figurative representation of the glory of the invisible God ( Matthew 17:2 I Timothy 6:16 ). Its use in this connection may refer to the first work of creation ( Genesis 1:3 ). 
 
    stretchest out the heavens--the visible heavens or sky which cover the earth as a curtain ( Isaiah 40:12 ).

title: Psalms 104:3
text:
3. in the waters--or, it may be "with"; using this fluid for the beams, or frames, of His residence accords with the figure of clouds for chariots, and wind as a means of conveyance. 
 
    walketh--or, "moveth" (compare  Psalms 18:10 Psalms 18:11 Amos 9:6 ).

title: Psalms 104:4
text:
4. This is quoted by Paul ( Hebrews 1:7 ) to denote the subordinate position of angels; that is, they are only messengers as other and material agencies. 
 
    spirits--literally, "winds." 
 
    flaming fire-- ( Psalms 105:32 ) being here so called.

title: Psalms 104:5
text: 5. The earth is firmly fixed by His power.

title: Psalms 104:6
text: 6-9. These verses rather describe the wonders of the flood than the creation ( Genesis 7:19 Genesis 7:20 II Peter 3:5 II Peter 3:6 ). God's method of arresting the flood and making its waters subside is poetically called a "rebuke" ( Psalms 76:6 Isaiah 50:2 ), and the process of the flood's subsiding by undulations among the hills and valleys is vividly described.

title: Psalms 104:10
text: 10-13. Once destructive, these waters are subjected to the service of God's creatures. In rain and dew from His chambers (compare  Psalms 104:3 ), and fountains and streams, they give drink to thirsting animals and fertilize the soil. Trees thus nourished supply homes to singing birds, and the earth teems with the productions of God's wise agencies,

title: Psalms 104:14
text:
14, 15. so that men and beasts are abundantly provided with food. 
 
    for the service--literally, "for the culture," &c., by which he secures the results. 
 
    oil ... shine--literally, "makes his face to shine more than oil," that is, so cheers and invigorates him, that outwardly he appears better than if anointed. 
 
    strengtheneth ... heart--gives vigor to man (compare  Judges 19:5 ).

title: Psalms 104:16
text: 16-19. God's care of even wild animals and uncultivated parts of the earth.

title: Psalms 104:20
text: 20-23. He provides and adapts to man's wants the appointed times and seasons.

title: Psalms 104:24
text: 24-26. From a view of the earth thus full of God's blessings, the writer passes to the sea, which, in its immensity, and as a scene and means of man's activity in commerce, and the home of countless multitudes of creatures, also displays divine power and beneficence. The mention of

title: Psalms 104:26
text: 26. leviathan-- ( Job 40:20 ) heightens the estimate of the sea's greatness, and of His power who gives such a place for sport to one of His creatures.

title: Psalms 104:27
text: 27-30. The entire dependence of this immense family on God is set forth. With Him, to kill or make alive is equally easy. To hide His face is to withdraw favor ( Psalms 13:1 ). By His spirit, or breath, or mere word, He gives life. It is His constant providence which repairs the wastes of time and disease.

title: Psalms 104:31
text: 31-34. While God could equally glorify His power in destruction, that He does it in preservation is of His rich goodness and mercy, so that we may well spend our lives in grateful praise, honoring to Him, and delightful to pious hearts ( Psalms 147:1 ).

title: Psalms 104:35
text:
35. Those who refuse such a protector and withhold such a service mar the beauty of His works, and must perish from His presence. 
 
    Praise ye the Lord--The Psalm closes with an invocation of praise, the translation of a Hebrew phrase, which is used as an English word, "Hallelujah," and may have served the purpose of a chorus, as often in our psalmody, or to give fuller expression to the writer's emotions. It is peculiar to Psalms composed after the captivity, as "Selah" is to those of an earlier date.

title: Psalms 105:1
text:
Psalms 105:1-45 . After an exhortation to praise God, addressed especially to the chosen people, the writer presents the special reason for praise, in a summary of their history from the calling of Abraham to their settlement in Canaan, and reminds them that their obedience was the end of all God's gracious dealings. 
 
    1. call ... name-- ( Psalms 79:6 Romans 10:13 ). Call on Him, according to His historically manifested glory. After the example of Abraham, who, as often as God acquired for Himself a name in guiding him, called in solemn worship upon the name of the Lord ( Genesis 12:8 Genesis 13:4 ). 
 
    among the people--or, "peoples" ( Psalms 18:49 ). 
 
    deeds--or, "wonders" ( Psalms 103:7 ).

title: Psalms 105:3
text:
3, 4. Seeking God's favor is the only true mode of getting true happiness, and His strength ( Psalms 105:4 ) is the only true source of protection (compare  Psalms 32:11 Psalms 40:16 ). 
 
    Glory ... name--boast in His perfections. The world glories in its horses and chariots against the Church of God lying in the dust; but our hope is in the name, that is, the power and love of God to His people, manifested in past deliverances.

title: Psalms 105:5
text: 5, 6. judgments ... mouth--His judicial decisions for the good and against the wicked.

title: Psalms 105:6
text: 6. chosen--rather qualifies "children" than "Jacob," as a plural.

title: Psalms 105:7
text: 7. Rather, "He, Jehovah, is our God." His title, "JEHOVAH," implies that He, the unchangeable, self-existing Being, makes things to be, that is, fulfils His promises, and therefore will not forsake His people. Though specially of His people, He is God over all.

title: Psalms 105:8
text:
8-11. The covenant was often ratified. 
 
    word--answering to "covenant" ( Psalms 105:9 ) in the parallel clause, namely, the word of promise, which, according to  Psalms 105:10 , He set forth for an inviolable law. 
 
    commanded--or, "ordained" ( Psalms 68:28 ). 
 
    to a thousand generations--perpetually. A verbal allusion to  Deuteronomy 7:9  (compare  Exodus 20:6 ).

title: Psalms 105:9
text: 9. Which covenant--or, "Word" ( Psalms 105:8 ).

title: Psalms 105:10
text: 10, 11. Alluding to God's promise to Jacob ( Genesis 28:13 ). Out of the whole storehouse of the promises of God, only one is prominently brought forward, namely, that concerning the possession of Canaan ( Psalms 105:11 ). Everything revolves around this. The wonders and judgments have all for their ultimate design the fulfilment of this promise.

title: Psalms 105:12
text:
12-15. few ... in number--alluding to Jacob's words ( Genesis 34:30 ), "I being few in number." 
 
    yea, very few--literally, "as a few," that is, like fewness itself (compare  Isaiah 1:9 ). 
 
    strangers--sojourners in the land of their future inheritance, as in a strange country ( Hebrews 11:9 ).

title: Psalms 105:13
text: 13. from one nation to another--and so from danger to danger; now in Egypt, now in the wilderness, and lastly in Canaan. Though a few strangers, wandering among various nations, God protected them.

title: Psalms 105:14
text: 14. reproved kings--Pharaoh of Egypt and Abimelech of Gerar ( Genesis 12:17 Genesis 20:3 ).

title: Psalms 105:15
text:
15. Touch not--referring to  Genesis 26:11 , where Abimelech says of Isaac, "He that toucheth this man or his wife shall surely be put to death." 
 
    mine anointed--as specially consecrated to Me ( Psalms 2:2 ). The patriarch was the prophet, priest, and king of his family. 
 
    my prophets--in a similar sense, compare  Genesis 20:7 . The "anointed" are those vessels of God, consecrated to His service, "in whom (as Pharaoh said of Joseph,  Genesis 41:38 ) the Spirit of God is" [HENGSTENBERG].

title: Psalms 105:16
text:
16. God ordered the famine. God 
 
    called for a famine--as if it were a servant, ready to come at God's bidding. Compare the centurion's words, as to disease being God's servant ( Matthew 8:8 Matthew 8:9 ). 
 
    upon the land--namely, Canaan ( Genesis 41:54 ). 
 
    staff of bread--what supports life ( Leviticus 26:26 Psalms 104:15 Isaiah 3:1 ).

title: Psalms 105:17
text: 17-21. Joseph was sent of God ( Genesis 45:5 ).

title: Psalms 105:18
text:
18. hurt with fetters-- ( Genesis 40:3 ). 
 
    was laid in iron--literally, "his soul" (see on  Psalms 16:9 ), or, "he came into iron," or, he was bound to his grief (compare  Psalms 3:2 Psalms 11:1 ). The "soul" is put for the whole person, because the soul of the captive suffers still more than the body. Joseph is referred to as being an appropriate type of those "bound in affliction and iron" ( Psalms 107:10 ).

title: Psalms 105:19
text:
19. his word came--His prophecy ( Genesis 41:11-20 ) to the officers came to pass, or was fulfilled ( Judges 13:12 Judges 13:17 I Samuel 9:6 , explain the form of speech). 
 
    the word of the Lord--or, "saying," or "decree of the Lord." 
 
    tried him--or, "proved him," by the afflictions it appointed him to endure before his elevation (compare  Genesis 41:40-43 ).

title: Psalms 105:22
text:
22. To bind--Not literally bind; but exercise over them absolute control, as the parallel in the second clause shows; also  Genesis 41:40 Genesis 41:44 , in which not literal fettering, but commanding obedience, is spoken of. It refers to  Psalms 105:18 . The soul that was once bound itself now binds others, even princes. The same moral binding is assigned to the saints ( Psalms 149:8 ). 
 
    teach ... senators wisdom--the ground of his exaltation by Pharaoh was his wisdom ( Genesis 41:39 ); namely, in state policy, and ordering well a kingdom.

title: Psalms 105:23
text:
23-25. Israel ... and Jacob--that is, Jacob himself is meant, as  Psalms 105:24  speaks of "his people." Still, he came with his whole house ( Genesis 46:6 Genesis 46:7 ). 
 
    sojourned-- ( Genesis 47:4 ). 
 
    land of Ham--or, Egypt ( Psalms 78:51 ).

title: Psalms 105:25
text: 25. turned their heart--God controls men's free acts (compare  I Samuel 10:9 ). "When Saul had turned his back to go from (God's prophet) Samuel, God turned (Margin) him another heart" (see  Exodus 1:8 , &c.).  Whatever evil the wicked man plots against God's people, God holds bound even his heart, so as not to lay a single plan except what God permits. Thus Isaiah ( Isaiah 43:17 ) says it was God who brought forth the army of Pharaoh to pursue Israel to their own destruction ( Exodus 4:21 Exodus 7:3 ).

title: Psalms 105:26
text: 26. Moses ... chosen--both what they were by divine choice ( Psalms 78:70 ).

title: Psalms 105:27
text: 27. signs--literally, "words of signs," or rather, as "words" in Hebrew means "things," "things of His signs," that is, His marvellous tokens of power ( Psalms 145:5 , Margin). Compare the same Hebraism ( Psalms 65:3 , Margin).

title: Psalms 105:28
text:
28-36. The ninth plague is made prominent as peculiarly wonderful.
